messages:
Anya: Quick sync — landing copy sprint for launch posts + webinar. Objective: one coherent top-level narrative that differentiates Hosted / Dedicated / Private, and clear inbound routing paths. Short timeline: drafts today, review tomorrow.
Mike: Love it. Conversion goal? Specific numbers help write microcopy.
Anya: Target: increase demo signups by 18% from current funnel, webinar signups +40% from baseline. Also want fewer misc support tickets from self-serve customers — clearer routing.
Sophia: Proposal — hero split: shared belief line, then three mode-specific subheads. Example shared: 'High-performance inference, wherever you run it.' Subheads: Hosted: 'Get started in minutes', Dedicated: 'Predictable throughput, reserved GPUs', Private: 'Bring inference behind your network.'
Riley: For CTAs, we should test two flows: (A) Primary CTA = "Start free API key" (self-serve), secondary = "Contact sales"; (B) Primary CTA = "Request a performance demo" for Dedicated/Private visitors, secondary = "Start free API key". Use routing param `deploy_mode` in forms.
Anya: Good. Also add microcopy under CTAs for pricing signal: small text "Usage-based billing, enterprise contracts available" for mid-funnel clarity.
Mike: Webinar promo microcopy draft: "Live benchmark walkthrough: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private — latency, cost, and reliability tradeoffs. Includes Q&A on migration paths." Add signup form with hidden field `interest=benchmarks`.
Sophia: Landing hero variants to A/B test (short): 1) "Production-grade inference, everywhere." 2) "Same API. Better economics. Any deployment." 3) "Ship LLM features with predictable latency and cost." Which do we prioritize?
Riley: My pick #2 — highlights unified API and economics. But keep #1 for enterprise-broad traffic.
Anya: Messaging for inbound routing: when form includes `deploy_mode=private` or keywords like "on-prem", route to Solutions AE; if `deploy_mode=hosted` route to Growth SDR and auto-send onboarding kit email.
Mike: Add a microcopy hint on Dedicated page: "Reserved capacity with SLA-backed latency targets" — helps sales qualify early.
Sophia: For SEO and benchmarks page, add H2: "Benchmarks — latency, cost per token, throughput" and include short copy: "Real workloads: batching, KV cache, quantization" to attract infra-focused searchers.
Anya: Quick UX ask for devex: include sample curl snippet in hero for Hosted and a small config snippet for Dedicated/Private showing `autoscale_policy` example.
Riley: Snippets:
```
# hosted quickstart
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" -d '{"model":"redwood-large","prompt":"Hello"}'
```
and
```
# dedicated config (example)
autoscale_policy: {min_nodes:2, max_nodes:10, cpu_threshold:0.6}
```
Anya: Can marketing ops wire up form routing and hidden fields today? We need inbound mapping in HubSpot: fields `deploy_mode`, `interest`, `benchmark_opt_in`.
marketing-bot: Reminder: draft due 24 hours. Links: kickoff doc https://docs.internal/redwood/landing-copy-sprint (internal). Use tag #landing-sprint.
Mike: I'll draft the 3 hero variants + CTA matrix by end of day and drop into the doc.
Sophia: I'll create the benchmark copy and the H2 list, plus sample images for the hero (latency graph, infra diagram).
Riley: I'll coordinate forms and HubSpot hidden fields, and add routing rules per `deploy_mode`.
Anya: Thanks team — sync tomorrow 10:30 to triage feedback. :rocket:
